c: Lionsgate pushed to cast Leonardo DiCaprio, so director Mary Harron was fired, then rehired after DiCaprio and Oliver Stone left the project.
Harron suggested Christian Bale go to a gym for the role, and he reportedly transformed within about two weeks.
Principal photography ran seven weeks on a $7 million budget, mostly in downtown Toronto. The office scenes were shot on a sound stage because building owners feared negative publicity.
Whitney Houston refused to let her recording of "The Greatest Love of All" be used, so an orchestral arrangement went in instead.
Victor Miller's screenplay was first titled A Long Night at Camp Blood.
The producers wanted Sally Field for Alice but couldn't afford her, so they held an open casting call.
Estelle Parsons was the first choice for Mrs. Voorhees but declined. Betsy Palmer took the role partly to pay for a new car.
Filming began in September 1979 at a working Boy Scout camp in Warren County, New Jersey. Unexpected snow forced a prologue scene indoors into a barn.
Tom Savini made a prosthetic head from Palmer's likeness for the decapitation shot, which was filmed without the actresses present.
Nicole Kidman was cast as Meg but left in early 2001 when a knee injury from Moulin Rouge! flared up. Jodie Foster replaced her and the role was rewritten to be stronger.
Cinematographer Darius Khondji was fired early in filming and replaced by Conrad W. Hall.
Production was suspended after studio executives disliked dailies in which Foster was concealing her pregnancy, and resumed once she had given birth.
The house and panic room were built on a Raleigh Studios soundstage for about $6 million, with three versions of the room constructed.
David Koepp drew on 2000 news coverage of safe rooms for the script, which he sold to Sony for $4 million.
Wes Craven built the story from a 1978 news item about two burglars who found children locked away in a Los Angeles house by their parents.
Craven feared Universal would reject a young Black lead and such a bizarre premise, but producers Tom Pollock and James Jacks backed the script.
Everett McGill and Wendy Robie were cast as the Robesons after playing the married couple Big Ed and Nadine on Twin Peaks.
Craven expected an NC-17, but the MPAA only asked for trims to one sequence, the one involving a gelatin liver prop.
Darren Aronofsky combined his viewings of Swan Lake with an unproduced screenplay, The Understudy, about being haunted by a double.
Aronofsky and Natalie Portman first discussed a ballet film in 2000, after Requiem for a Dream.
Portman and Mila Kunis trained for about six months before filming to build bodies closer to professional dancers.
American Ballet Theatre soloists Sarah Lane and María Riccetto served as the dance doubles for Portman and Kunis.
It was shot on Super 16mm in New York City from late 2009, with a grainy look meant to echo The Wrestler.
Jalmari Helander's planned follow-up was the sci-fi comedy Jerry and Ms. Universe, but the COVID-19 pandemic led him to make Sisu instead.
Sisu was shot in 2021 near Nuorgam village in Utsjoki, Lapland, on a budget of about €6 million.
Helander has said First Blood and the Finnish sniper Simo Häyhä inspired the film.
